default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1088.title: Stochastic re-entry from the extreme
E-1088.hypothesis: When the close-in-range oscillator leaves its oversold/overbought zone, the stretched side has run out of aggressors and the snap-back has room; fade the exit from the zone.

E-1089.title: Channel midpoint cross
E-1089.hypothesis: A close across the midpoint of the previous N-minute high/low channel shows that buyers or sellers took the middle of the recent auction; follow the cross.

E-1090.title: Regression-slope t-stat trend start
E-1090.hypothesis: When the least-squares slope of the recent closes becomes statistically steep, a persistent order flow (metaorder) is working; follow the first crossing of the t threshold.

E-1091.title: Narrowest-range bar break
E-1091.hypothesis: The narrowest bar of the last N bars marks a pause in two-sided trade; a close beyond its high or low releases the compressed order flow.

E-1092.title: Round-number rejection
E-1092.hypothesis: Limit orders cluster at round index levels; a bar that touches one and closes back on the other side shows the resting orders held, so trade away from the level.

E-1093.title: Bar-open gap follow
E-1093.hypothesis: A bar opening beyond the previous bar's extreme by a fraction of the typical range means a sweep of resting liquidity between bars; if it also closes in that direction, follow.

E-1094.title: Volume build-up run
E-1094.hypothesis: Several consecutive bars with rising volume and rising closes, above the usual volume for the hour, show participation growing with the move; follow it.

E-1095.title: Prior-session midpoint cross
E-1095.hypothesis: The midpoint of yesterday's range is the fair value many desks anchor to; a close through it with a small buffer signals that today is taking value in that direction.

E-1096.title: Short-term volatility expansion follow
E-1096.hypothesis: When the short-term return volatility jumps above its own recent norm, new information is being priced; follow the direction of the move that came with it.

E-1097.title: Keltner band re-entry fade
E-1097.hypothesis: A close outside the EMA plus/minus a multiple of the average bar range is an overextension; the first close back inside the band marks exhausted momentum, so fade it.
